children: Commodity markets traded mixed on September 21, with oil prices declining as investors assessed prospects of recovering Saudi shipments amid heightened Middle East tensions, while gold held steady as traders weighed persistent inflation risks and the outlook for interest rates following the US Federal Reserve’s first rate hike since 2023.

Oil prices slid on Monday as investors eyed a recovery in shipments from Saudi Arabia despite ongoing attacks by Yemeni Houthis that have escalated tension in the Middle East while the US and Iran remain in a stalemate.
Brent crude futures dropped 81 cents, or 0.78%, to $103.06 a barrel after settling down 0.91% on Friday.
US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $99.41 a barrel, down 89 cents, or 0.89%, following a 1.58% loss in the previous session.
In precious metals, gold was steady as traders weighed the risk of persistent inflation and the path for interest rates after the Federal Reserve’s first hike since 2023.

Bullion was trading around $4,375 an ounce, after posting a moderate gain the week before. Several Fed policymakers are due to speak publicly this week after voting unanimously to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point at their Sept.
Silver rose 0.2% to $66.38 an ounce. Platinum and palladium edged higher.
The dollar was quoted in a tight range against Group-of-10 peers in early trading into a week that includes leaders’ meetings during the United Nations General Assembly.

title: Commodity Corner: Oil prices slip, gold holds steady amid inflation, rate concerns
